newsitem.title: USA: Mallon reserves rose 25 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Mallon reserves rose 25 pct in 1996.

text.p: Mallon Resources Corp said Friday its proved oil and natural gas reserves at year-end 1996 were 6.4 million barrels of oil equivalent, a 25 percent increase over the 5.1 million barrels a year earlier.

The present value of its year-end 1996 reserves (discounted to present value using a 10 percent discount and assuming flat year-end prices) increased 138 percent to $50.0 million from the $21.0 million at year-end 1995.
Mallon said its proved reserves are 27 percent oil and 73 percent natural gas.

This increase was driven by the company's "development drilling operations on our core southeast New Mexico properties. Just 20 percent of the increase was attributable to higher oil and gas prices," the company said.
"We are particularly pleased because the results were achieved despite the fact that our drilling program was capital constrained until late in the year.

"We expect even better results in 1997, as the company begins to realize the benefits of its accelerated drilling programs in the Delaware and San Juan Basins," Mallon continued. "With the completion of our equity financing in October 1996, we have sharply increased our drilling and workover activity in New Mexico.

"This ramp-up in activity will continue to improve both production and financial results during the year. As a result, Mallon expects to report another significant increase in our 1997 year-end reserves," it said.
